title: The Lyman-Alpha Forest and Intergalactic Absorption as Tests of the Bounce Frame

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Athena Romano, and this is The Lyman-Alpha Forest and Intergalactic Absorption as Tests of the Bounce Frame. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Athena Romano, and this is The Lyman-Alpha Forest and Intergalactic Absorption as Tests of the Bounce Frame. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'The Redshift Equivalent of the Bounce Density and the Resulting Bound on All Forest Observables'. Its stated result: Headline computed outcome for this study: z_bounce = 1.5350960704735478e+28; log10_z_bounce = 28.19; frac_at_z5 = 5.9709999999999995e-83; result = negative: bounce density corresponds to redshift ~1e28; all forest observables insensitive.
Now we go one step further into the material.

'The Column-Density Distribution of Forest Absorbers: Slope Recovery and a Bounce Null'. Its stated result: Headline computed outcome for this study: beta_recovered = 1.5; expected_beta_input = 1.5; bounce_beta_shift = 1.769185185185185e-83; result = slope recovered; bounce contributes no measurable tilt (negative).
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'The Doppler Parameter Distribution of Forest Lines: Thermal Widths, Turbulent Excess, and a Bounce Null'. Its stated result: Headline computed outcome for this study: b_thermal_at_10000K = 12.85; result = observed widths require non-thermal broadening; bounce supplies none (negative). All values were computed from stated assumptions and published input values, not measured, and the deposit was verified by read-back against the public record (exact title, sole creator William Alexander Aldred with ORCID 0009-0000-1215-577X, CC BY 4.0 licenc
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'The Effective Optical Depth Power Law of Intergalactic Absorption and Its Insensitivity to a High-Density Bounce'. Its stated result: Headline computed outcome for this study: gamma = 3.255; bounce_gamma_shift = 5.759545688385696e-83; result = negative: fitted slope shift from bounce is negligible. All values were computed from stated assumptions and published input values, not measured, and the deposit was verified by read-back against the public record (exact title, sole creator William Alexander Aldred with ORCID 0009-0000-1215-577X, CC BY 4.0 l
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Variance and Shape of the Transmitted-Flux Probability Distribution as a Forest Diagnostic'. Its stated result: Headline computed outcome for this study: mean_flux_from_pdf = 0.436; variance = 0.0866; skewness = 0.272; bounce_variance_shift = 1.532185137777778e-84; result = PDF moments recovered; bounce shift negligible (negative).
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'The Small-Scale Cutoff of the One-Dimensional Flux Power Spectrum as a Thermal and Bounce Test'. Its stated result: Headline computed outcome for this study: k_cut_T10000 = 0.0778; bounce_kc_shift_fraction = 1.769185185185185e-83; result = thermal cutoff dominates; bounce shift negligible (negative for bounce). All values were computed from stated assumptions and published input values, not measured, and the deposit was verified by read-back against the public record (exact title, sole creator William Alexander Aldred with ORCID 0
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “The Redshift Equivalent of the Bounce Density and the Resulting Bound on All Forest Observables”. Its stated result is: Headline computed outcome for this study: z_bounce = 1.5350960704735478e+28; log10_z_bounce = 28.19; frac_at_z5 = 5.9709999999999995e-83; result = negative: bounce density corresponds to redshift ~1e28; all forest observables insensitive. (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'The Redshift Equivalent of the Bounce Density and the Resulting Bound on All Forest Observables'; 'The Column-Density Distribution of Forest Absorbers: Slope Recovery and a Bounce Null'; 'The Doppler Parameter Distribution of Forest Lines: Thermal Widths, Turbulent Excess, and a Bounce Null'; 'The Effective Optical Depth Power Law of Intergalactic Absorption and Its Insensitivity to a High-Density Bounce'; 'Variance and Shape of the Transmitted-Flux Probability Distribution as a Forest Diagnostic'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

And here is that same result with the words stripped away — just the quantities standing in a row: z_bounce = 1.5350960704735478e+28; log10_z_bounce = 28.19; frac_at_z5 = 5.9709999999999995e-83. (4) In that row, z_bounce stands beside 1.5350960704735478e+28 — so the answer the lesson gives is 1.5350960704735478e+28. Now it is yours: say that value, in any honest form.
